name: Huxley-Gödel Machine: Human-Level Coding Agent Development by an Approximation of the Optimal Self-Improving Machine
authors: Wenyi Wang, Piotr Piękos (equal contribution), Li Nanbo, Firas Laakom, Yimeng Chen, Mateusz Ostaszewski, Mingchen Zhuge, Jürgen Schmidhuber; lead affiliation King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), Thuwal, Saudi Arabia
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2510.21614, cs.AI, submitted 24 Oct 2025, v3 29 Oct 2025); also under review (OpenReview id T0EiEuhOOL, likely ICLR 2026 submission)
feedback_source: external-tool (execution-grounded software-engineering benchmark evaluation: agent-task pass/fail outcomes on SWE-bench and Polyglot tasks). The self-modification proposals are produced by an LLM coding agent editing its own codebase; the improvement signal comes from benchmark task success indicators aggregated over a clade, not from a learned critic or human feedback.
iteration_structure: population/evolutionary tree-search. Self-improvement is formalized as an iterative tree-search problem: from an initial root agent, a tree (archive) of self-modified agents is grown. A compound policy decides at each step whether to expand (generate a self-modified child agent) or evaluate (run an existing agent on one more task). Expansion is guided by Thompson Sampling over clade-metaproductivity (CMP) estimates with an exploration-exploitation scheduler; expansion vs. evaluation timing follows a UCB-Air-style infinite-armed-bandit rule (expand when N_t^alpha >= |T_t|, alpha=0.6). Decoupled, asynchronous (HGM-Async) execution across CPUs.
reflection_object: agent's own code/architecture. Each node is a coding agent (a full software-engineering project / scaffolding) that edits its own codebase to produce a self-modified child agent. The thing being reflected on/modified is the agent's own code and tool/scaffold architecture (self-referential self-modification). The underlying LLM backbone weights are NOT updated.
learning_locus: in_context_verbal (no weight update). Despite the item-level 'gradient_weight_update' tag, the method itself performs NO gradient/weight updates: it is a non-gradient, search-based self-improvement that mutates agent code via LLM-driven edits and selects via clade-aggregated benchmark outcomes. The LLM weights (GPT-5/GPT-5-mini, Qwen3-Coder) are frozen throughout; learning is encoded entirely in the evolved agent code/scaffold and the search archive.
requires_training: none. No SFT, RL, or preference training of the model is performed. Improvement is achieved purely through LLM-driven code self-modification guided by a bandit search; the LLM backbones remain frozen.
reward_or_critic_model: verifiable reward. The improvement signal is the binary success/failure of an agent on benchmark coding tasks (execution-grounded, repeatable trials), aggregated into the Clade-Metaproductivity (CMP) estimator CMP_hat(a) = n_success^C(a) / (n_success^C(a) + n_failure^C(a)). No trained reward model, no LLM-as-judge, no separate retrospective model.
distillation_target: agent code/scaffold (reusable artifact). The improvements are distilled into the evolved coding-agent's own source code / scaffolding (the discovered best-belief agent), which is a reusable, transferable artifact (it transfers across datasets SWE-Verified->SWE-Lite and across LLMs GPT-5-mini->GPT-5). It is not distilled into model-weights, episodic memory, or a constitution. The persistent search archive (tree of agents with success/failure counts) is an additional artifact guiding selection.
emergent_vs_engineered: engineered. The self-improvement loop, CMP estimator, Thompson-sampling expansion policy, and asynchronous scheduler are an explicitly engineered search scaffold/algorithm wrapped around frozen LLMs. The reflective self-modification behavior is produced by prompting an LLM coding agent to edit its own code; it is not an RL-emergent reasoning behavior of the base model.
memory_type: structured-notes/graph (a tree/archive of evolved agents). The archive T_t is a tree of self-modified agents, each annotated with the number of passed/failed task evaluations (n_success, n_failure); this serves as the population memory that the search policy reads to compute clade-metaproductivity and to select agents to expand/evaluate.
memory_persistence: cross-task. Within a single self-improvement run, the agent archive (tree) persists and accumulates evaluation evidence across many tasks and across iterations of self-modification. The discovered agent then transfers cross-task/cross-model at deployment (SWE-Verified->SWE-Lite, GPT-5-mini->GPT-5), but there is no production cross-session online memory described.
memory_curation_mechanism: population-or-Pareto-selected (clade-aggregated, append-only tree with bandit-guided selection). The tree of agents is grown append-only, but selection of which nodes to expand/evaluate is governed by Thompson sampling over clade-metaproductivity, so unpromising lineages are deprioritized and early-stopped; the final returned agent is the 'best-belief' agent (highest epsilon-percentile of the utility posterior). This concentrates compute on promising clades rather than retaining/exploring all uniformly.
error_localization_granularity: agent-level (node/clade-level in the search tree). The corrective/selection signal operates at the granularity of whole agents and their clades (lineages): an agent's promise is judged by aggregating descendant outcomes (CMP), and evaluation is done at the single agent-task-pair granularity. There is no step-level or token-level error localization; the self-modification edits to code are proposed holistically by the LLM coding agent.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: inter-task. Experience (benchmark outcomes) is aggregated across many tasks and across the lineage of self-modifications to guide which agent to evolve next; the goal is to discover an agent that generalizes across downstream tasks, not to refine a single task's output in place.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: avoidance-only. Improvement happens across generations of self-modified agents (a better child agent replaces/outperforms its parent in expectation); there is no in-flight mid-trajectory recovery within a single task episode. The mechanism is to seed/select more productive lineages and prune stagnant ones, and to early-stop unpromising agents.
task_domains: code (autonomous software-engineering / coding-agent development). Self-improving coding agents that fix real-world GitHub issues and solve programming challenges.
benchmarks: SWE-bench Verified (SWE-Verified, 500 tasks; 60-task subset SWE-Verified-60), SWE-bench Lite (SWE-Lite, 300 tasks), and Polyglot (Aider Polyglot coding problems). Comparison also references the swebench.com SWE-Lite leaderboard.
headline_result: Optimized on SWE-bench Verified (500 tasks, 8000 evaluations) with GPT-5-mini, HGM discovers an agent solving 61.4% of SWE-Verified tasks (up from a 53.2% initial agent), the top GPT-5-mini-based system and top-10 overall on the leaderboard. The HGM-discovered agent transferred to SWE-bench Lite with GPT-5 reaches 57.0% (standard) / 47.8% (filtered), matching the best officially checked human-engineered coding agent (SWE-agent: 56.7% standard / 48.3% filtered) i.e. human-level coding-agent performance.
baselines: Prior self-improving coding-agent development methods: Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM, Zhang et al. 2025a) and Self-Improving Coding Agent (SICA, Robeyns et al. 2025); shared identical initial agent (from DGM's official implementation). For human comparison: best officially checked human-engineered coding agents on the SWE-bench leaderboards, notably SWE-agent (Yang et al. 2024), and SWE-agent+GPT-5-mini / SWE-agent+Claude-4-Sonnet adaptations.
gains_vs_baseline: Self-improving capability (best-belief agent, same 800-evaluation budget, same initial agent at 40% SWE-Verified-60 / 20.3% Polyglot): SWE-Verified-60 HGM 56.7% (+16.7) vs DGM 53.3% (+13.3) vs SICA 50.0% (+10); Polyglot HGM 30.5% (+10.2) vs DGM 27.1% (+6.8) vs SICA 25.4% (+5.1). Generalization to SWE-Lite (filtered/standard): HGM agent 40.1%/49.0% vs initial ancestor 34.8%/44.0% and vs SWE-agent+GPT-5-mini 39.6%/47.6%. With GPT-5 transfer, HGM agent 47.8%/57.0% vs best leaderboard SWE-agent 48.3%/56.7%. CMP-estimator fidelity (Pearson, weighted/unweighted): SWE-Verified-60 HGM 0.778/0.512 vs DGM 0.285/0.406 vs SICA 0.444/0.444; Polyglot HGM 0.626/0.873 vs DGM 0.383/0.357 vs SICA 0.274/0.274.
compute_cost_profile: Training/search cost is measured in allocated CPU-hours for a fixed budget of 800 task evaluations (with the same initial agent and backbones). HGM is markedly more efficient than baselines: SWE-Verified-60 HGM 517 hours vs DGM 1231 hours (2.38x faster; SICA entered an infinite loop / context-window errors after ~360 evaluations); Polyglot HGM 347 hours vs DGM 2385 hours (6.86x faster) and vs SICA 572 hours (1.65x faster). Efficiency comes from asynchronous decoupling of expansion and evaluation and single-agent-task-pair evaluations enabling early stopping. Backbones: GPT-5 (expansion) + GPT-5-mini (evaluation) for SWE; Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct (expansion) + Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct (evaluation) for Polyglot. The full-scale run used 8000 evaluations on 500 SWE-Verified tasks. No per-token inference multiplier is reported.
known_limitations: Stated limitations and caveats: (1) Theoretical equivalence to the Gödel Machine holds only under Assumption 1 (objective is a function of only the final agent; repeatable trials with time/event-independent outcomes; each self-modification costs exactly one budget unit; only self-modification incurs time cost) — a much more restricted setting than the original single-life Gödel Machine. (2) HGM only approximates CMP via a clade-aggregated empirical estimator; it does not have the true CMP oracle. (3) Authors caution that higher leaderboard scores do not necessarily indicate superior general coding ability, since both human- and machine-designed agents may overfit to the benchmark. (4) Results are confined to coding-agent/software-engineering tasks and to specific LLM backbones (GPT-5 family, Qwen3-Coder). (5) No model-weight learning — improvement is bounded by what the frozen LLMs can express via code edits.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: external-tool/verifier. The method depends fundamentally on execution-grounded, repeatable benchmark evaluations (task pass/fail) as the improvement signal — it is not intrinsic self-verification. It does NOT use ground-truth output labels or hidden test results for the agent under test in the Polyglot setting (following DGM, agents have no access to private test cases/results there), but it does rely on benchmark task-success outcomes as a verifiable external reward to estimate metaproductivity.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive (task-dependent on benchmark feedback). Using clade-metaproductivity guidance, HGM reliably produces agents that improve over their initial ancestor and over DGM/SICA on every reported benchmark, and these gains transfer to unseen tasks and larger models (evidence against mere overfitting). The improvement requires external benchmark (verifiable) feedback; the paper's central contribution is precisely that immediate benchmark performance is an unreliable selection signal (the Metaproductivity-Performance Mismatch), which clade-level aggregation corrects.
calibration_effect: not-measured. The paper does not study reasoning-model confidence calibration or a 'reasoning tax'; it concerns selection-criterion fidelity (CMP estimation correlation), not probabilistic calibration of model outputs.
failure_attribution_capability: n/a. HGM is a self-improvement/agent-design method, not a failure-attribution method; it does not produce a failure-mode taxonomy or attribute responsibility to agents/steps. It does, however, diagnose a meta-level pathology — the Metaproductivity-Performance Mismatch (MPM) — i.e., that benchmark score is a misleading proxy for self-improvement potential.
failure_mode_addressed: The core failure mode targeted is the Metaproductivity-Performance Mismatch (MPM): greedy selection by immediate benchmark performance can pick high-scoring agents that seed stagnating lineages while overlooking lower-scoring agents that seed productive self-improvement lineages. Related inefficiency addressed: baselines (DGM/SICA) conflate expansion and evaluation so a newly created agent monopolizes evaluations (e.g., an agent failing nine tasks keeps consuming evaluations) — HGM fixes this via decoupled, single-agent-task-pair evaluation with early stopping. No mapping to MAST's multi-agent failure taxonomy is provided.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new dataset/benchmark released. The paper releases code at https://github.com/metauto-ai/HGM and the discovered/optimized coding agents; evaluation uses existing benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified/Lite, Polyglot).
builds_on: Gödel Machine (Schmidhuber 2003) and self-referential learning (Schmidhuber 1987); Success-Story Algorithm (Schmidhuber & Zhao 1996); Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM, Zhang et al. 2025a); Self-Improving Coding Agent (SICA, Robeyns et al. 2025); Self-Taught Optimizer / STOP (Zelikman et al. 2024) and Gödel Agent (Yin et al. 2024); Huxley's (1957) notion of clade; SWE-agent (Yang et al. 2024) and SWE-bench (Jimenez et al. 2024); bandit/search foundations: Thompson Sampling (Agrawal & Goyal 2012; Chapelle & Li 2011), UCB-Air infinite-armed bandits (Wang et al. 2008), fixed-budget BAI and MCTS/UCT.
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited by (Semantic Scholar, ~16 citing papers): Live-SWE-agent (Xia et al., self-evolving SWE agent on the fly), MemEvolve: Meta-Evolution of Agent Memory Systems (Zhang et al.), AEvo / Harnessing Agentic Evolution (Zhang et al.), EvoFSM: Controllable Self-Evolution for Deep Research with Finite State Machines, Evolutionary Ensemble of Agents (EvE), Search over Self-Edit Strategies for LLM Adaptation (Cheong et al.), AutoEnv (Zhang et al.), Pioneer Agent (Atreja et al.), SE-Bench and SWE-EVO (benchmarks for self-evolution / long-horizon software evolution).
citation_count: 16 (Semantic Scholar, as of June 2026; 2 highly-influential citations)
reasoning_model_native: false. HGM does not require or rely on built-in-reflection reasoning models (o1/R1-style); it wraps frozen general LLMs (GPT-5, GPT-5-mini, Qwen3-Coder) in an external code-self-modification + bandit-search scaffold. Reflection/improvement is engineered at the agent-code/search level, not native to the model.
on_policy_distillation_link: No on-policy distillation. HGM performs no policy distillation or weight updates; improvements are distilled into evolved agent code/scaffolds via search rather than into model weights. Conceptually adjacent to skill/scaffold optimization (the discovered agent is a reusable skill artifact) and to population-based search, but it is explicitly a non-gradient, LLM-reflection-and-code-update learning mechanism (as characterized for its predecessor SICA).
sample_efficiency: Reported in number of benchmark task evaluations (and allocated CPU-hours) rather than gradient steps. Self-improving-capability comparison used a budget of 800 evaluations; the full SWE-Verified optimization used 8000 evaluations to reach 61.4%. HGM is substantially more sample/compute efficient than DGM and SICA at fixed budget (2.38x faster than DGM on SWE-Verified-60; 6.86x faster than DGM and 1.65x faster than SICA on Polyglot), attributed to clade-aggregated estimates (more samples per decision), decoupled single-agent-task-pair evaluation with early stopping, and asynchronous parallelism.
